findings.plain_summary: OPM tells agencies it will reissue classification and qualification standards for 600+ occupational series in 22 cycles of about 30 series each starting FY2027, built on validated skills and AI-assisted, human-validated workflows. Each cycle gives agencies 120 days to apply the new standards to new and reclassified positions and 365 days to review all existing positions in covered series, with completion reporting to OPM.
could_not_determine: How many positions or employees are affected across the 600+ series
Which occupational series fall in which cycle, or the exact FY2027 start date and cycle intervals
Cost or staffing resources for agencies to carry out the reviews, and whether any funding is provided
Consequences for agencies that miss the 120-day or 365-day deadlines
Format and content of the required completion report to OPM
Whether the 22 cycles have a defined end date (the memo says 'and continuing beyond')
Specific criteria OPM will use to decide that a labor-market signal warrants a modular interim update

findings.plain_summary: OPM confirms that its direct final rule requiring FLSA claims to be filed through the eFile system took effect September 29, 2026, after finding that none of the eight comments was a significant adverse comment. The notice also makes several commitments on how OPM will handle eFile exemption requests, outages and late filings, and it declines commenters' requests for tolling, dual-track paper filing and fixed response deadlines.

items.headline: OPM declines to toll deadlines during pending eFile exemption requests
items.what_changes: OPM rejected Comment 03's proposed text that would automatically toll deadlines while an exemption request is pending, or treat a non-electronic filing as timely once an exemption issues. A claimant's back-pay recovery date still depends on when OPM or the agency receives the claim, so delay in obtaining an exemption can affect recoverable back pay. OPM instead promises case-by-case consideration of timely good-faith contact.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM therefore declines to adopt Comment 03's proposed regulatory text automatically tolling a deadline during the pendency of an exemption request, or deeming a non-electronic submission filed as of its original date once an exemption later issues
items.section: Filing-Method Changes and the FLSA Limitations Period

items.headline: Exemption requests may be made by phone or email, treated the same as website requests
items.what_changes: Although the codified text says to request an exemption as instructed on OPM's website, OPM states that claimants may request an exemption by the telephone number or email in the contact caption of the DFR or a successor document. OPM will treat timely telephone or written requests the same as website requests. This is an OPM statement in the preamble, not new regulatory text.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: a party or representative may request an exemption under Sec.  551.710(b)(7) by contacting OPM using the telephone number or email address listed in the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT caption of the DFR or of any successor document
items.section: The Discretionary Exemption From Electronic Filing

items.headline: OPM rejects fixed response deadlines, outage tolling, and dual-track paper filing
items.what_changes: OPM did not adopt Comment 04's twelve requested text additions, Comment 07's permanent dual-track paper/email intake for field and wage-grade staff, its fixed outage tolling, or any fixed response deadline for exemption requests. OPM says claims circumstances vary too widely for numerical rules. Exemptions stay in OPM's discretion.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM has not adopted Comment 04's twelve requested textual additions or Comment 07's proposed fixed, non-discretionary dual-track and outage-tolling provisions or a fixed response deadline for exemption requests.
items.section: The Discretionary Exemption From Electronic Filing

items.headline: eFile outages and access barriers will be weighed in reconsideration and waiver decisions
items.what_changes: OPM says a documented agency-side eFile outage, and a claimant's literacy, disability or other barrier to using eFile, will bear on whether a cancelled claim is reconsidered under 551.707(b) or the 45-day period is waived under 551.708(a). This is discretionary and case-by-case, not codified.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM will likewise treat a documented, agency-side outage of the eFile system, and a claimant's literacy, disability, or other barrier to independently using the eFile system, as circumstances bearing on whether reconsideration of a cancelled claim is warranted under Sec.  551.707(b) or whether the 45-day period in Sec.  551.708(a) should be waived.
items.section: The Discretionary Exemption From Electronic Filing

items.headline: Rule held procedural; limitations periods said to be unchanged, with an acknowledged effect on receipt date
items.what_changes: OPM defends issuing the rule without notice and comment under the procedural-rule exception, saying it changes only the method of submission. OPM concedes a filing method could in an individual case affect the date a claim is received, but says this does not alter the length of any limitations period. It also says the good-cause alternative need not be reached.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The possibility that a change in filing method could, in an individual case, affect the date on which a claim is received does not convert a rule about filing methods into a rule about the length of a limitations period.
items.section: Filing-Method Changes and the FLSA Limitations Period

items.headline: Preamble's "45 days" effective-date language was a drafting error; September 29, 2026 controls
items.what_changes: OPM admits the original DFR preamble inconsistently said the rule would take effect 45 days after the comment period closed. OPM confirms September 29, 2026 as the effective date. Claims filed before that date are processed under the old requirements; later submissions must comply with the new ones.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The reference to ``45 days'' was a drafting error.

items.headline: eFile information collection approved with revised burden estimate
items.what_changes: OMB approved the eFile information collection under control number 3206-0282, not the "3206-NEW" the commenters cited. The revised burden estimate is 1,286 respondents and 13,039 annual burden hours, covering all appeal types in eFile. OPM says it did not refuse or delay any claim or exemption request because of control-number status.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The 30-day notice (91 FR 46802 (July 24, 2026)) reflects a revised estimate of 1,286 respondents and 13,039 annual burden hours, which reflects the full scope of appeals available through the eFile system.
items.section: Paperwork Reduction Act Status of the eFile Information Collection

items.headline: Electronic service: eFile registration is consent, and monitoring is the claimant's duty
items.what_changes: OPM answers Comment 03 that registering as an eFiler constitutes consent to electronic service and that monitoring case activity is like reviewing mail. A technical system failure that prevented receipt of a posting will be weighed case by case under existing discretion, not by a new rule.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Registration as an eFiler constitutes consent to electronic service.

items.headline: Claimants under negotiated grievance procedures are unaffected
items.what_changes: Claimants covered at any time during the claim period by a collective bargaining agreement that does not exclude FLSA matters must use the negotiated grievance procedure. Sections 551.704-551.710, including the eFiling provisions, do not apply to them.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The filing-method changes addressed in this notice accordingly have no bearing on claimants who are subject to a negotiated grievance procedure that does not exclude FLSA matters.
items.section: Claimants Subject to a Negotiated Grievance Procedure

items.headline: OPM rejects bargaining duty and Regulations.gov, 508, Privacy Act and FISMA challenges
items.what_changes: OPM says it has no duty to bargain over this governmentwide rule, citing 5 U.S.C. 7117(a)(1). It finds no basis to reopen comment over alleged Regulations.gov display problems. It treats 508, Privacy Act and FISMA compliance as independent obligations that would not make the rule substantive, and notes the eFile cloud services are FedRAMP-certified.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: under 5 U.S.C. 7117(a)(1), the duty to bargain does not extend to matters that are the subject of a Government-wide rule or regulation, such as the regulations in 5 CFR part 551 that OPM issues under 29 U.S.C. 204(f).
items.section: Section 508, the Privacy Act, FISMA, and Collective Bargaining Obligations

could_not_determine: How many FLSA claimants or representatives are affected by mandatory eFiling, or how many exemptions have been requested or granted.
How long OPM will take to act on an exemption request; OPM declined to set any deadline.
The identity or affiliation of the eight commenters (comments are identified only by number).
Whether the eFile rule has been challenged in court.
Any cost or savings estimate for the rule beyond the 1,286-respondent and 13,039-hour burden figures.

findings.plain_summary: OPM issues a standing Super Intelligence (SI)-Assisted Position Review Toolkit that gives agencies a methodology, three prompt sets, and guardrails for reviewing position descriptions against the updated Competency Based Classification Standard under the RCRQ initiative. Use of SI is optional and tool-agnostic, but the memo sets documentation, human-review, and data-handling expectations for any SI-assisted review and says OPM can expand the toolkit without reissuing a memo.

items.headline: Guardrails on SI use: data restrictions, named human reviewer, and record retention
items.what_changes: Agencies are asked not to put PII or non-public data into SI tools not approved under their own governance, privacy, and records policies. They must document a human reviewer of record for each determination informed by SI output and retain prompts and outputs as part of the classification record. The memo says the toolkit's guardrails apply to any SI-assisted review under these standards, not just the toolkit's prompts.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote:
Document the human reviewer of record 
for every determination informed by an SI-assisted output and retain prompts and 
outputs as part of the classification record.
items.section: Use of the Toolkit by Your Agency

items.headline: SI output cannot set series, title, or grade; classification specialists lead
items.what_changes: SI tooling is limited to triage and prioritization. Classification specialists lead, with I-O psychologists, HR advisors and subject-matter experts, and must validate any SI-assisted output before acting on it.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote:
The tooling
[[Page 3]]
3 
 
supports triage and prioritization; it does not set series, title, or grade.
items.section: Use of the Toolkit by Your Agency

items.headline: SI use is recommended but optional and tool-agnostic
items.what_changes: OPM recommends SI-enabled review for large volumes of position descriptions but does not require it, does not prescribe tools, and offers the methodology and prompts as options.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote:
OPM is not prescriptive on the use of SI for this 
review and is SI-agnostic as to the tools agencies select.

items.headline: OPM can expand the toolkit without reissuing any memo
items.what_changes: The toolkit is a standing product that OPM will revise and expand based on agency experience, and such revisions do not require reissuing a memorandum, so agencies must track toolkit updates themselves.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote:
OPM will expand the toolkit based on 
agencies' experience applying the prompts it contains and the experiences they report, 
so that the toolkit continues to meet agency needs; such revisions do not require 
reissuance of any memorandum.

items.headline: Review starts from existing job analyses and is prioritized by divergence, incumbents, and hiring volume
items.what_changes: Agencies are asked to treat the most recent job analysis for each covered position as the starting point, map it to the updated standard, and document the crosswalk as the record supporting each classification determination. They should sequence review by divergence from the standard, incumbent population, and hiring volume rather than in arbitrary order. The memo says the toolkit creates no new implementation tasks.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote:
Apply the prompt sets to 
prioritize positions by divergence from the standard, by incumbent population, and 
by hiring volume, rather than reviewing the inventory in arbitrary order.
items.section: Use of the Toolkit by Your Agency

items.headline: Existing skills-based practices count toward implementation and should not be duplicated
items.what_changes: The toolkit includes a statement that competency models, validated assessments, rewritten vacancy announcements, and prior job analyses already held by agencies count toward implementation.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote:
A statement of the skills-based practices agencies already hold — competency 
models, validated assessments, rewritten vacancy announcements, and prior job 
analyses — that count toward implementation and should not be duplicated.

could_not_determine: The text of the toolkit itself (the prompt sets and the full guardrails) is an attachment not included in the document.
How many agencies, positions, or employees are affected is not stated.
No deadlines or cycle dates for position review are given; they are left to separate cycle memoranda.
No cost, funding, or resource information for agencies is provided.
Which SI tools are approved is not stated; approval is left to each agency's own SI governance policies.

findings.plain_summary: OPM confirms that its July 31, 2026 direct final rule, which requires claimants to file certain administrative claims through the eFile system unless OPM grants an exemption, took effect September 29, 2026. OPM found none of the five comments to be significant adverse, made no change to the rule text, and used the preamble to clarify how it will apply the exemption, good-cause, and denying-official provisions.

items.headline: Mandatory eFile with discretionary exemption; late-filing risk if no exemption requested
items.what_changes: OPM may exempt a party from eFiling in its sole and exclusive discretion, and will not find good cause for a late filing if the party failed to ask for an exemption before the deadline. All five commenters objected. OPM kept the provision without fixed criteria, response deadline, or reconsideration process, but said it applies a 'cannot reasonably file electronically' standard.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM confirms that the standard governing exemption requests is the one described in the DFR's preamble: an exemption is available to ``a party or representative who cannot reasonably file electronically.''
items.section: II. Public Comment Analysis – The Discretionary Exemption From Electronic Filing

items.headline: OPM adds phone/email exemption requests and good-cause factors, but only as preamble statements
items.what_changes: Exemption requests may be made by the telephone number or email in the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT caption, not only through OPM's website, and are treated the same as website requests. OPM will also treat eFile outages and claimant literacy, disability, or other barriers as bearing on good cause. These are statements of practice; no regulatory text changed.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM will treat a timely telephone or written exemption request the same as one submitted through OPM's website. OPM will likewise treat a documented, agency-side outage of the eFile system, and a claimant's literacy, disability, or other barrier to independently using the eFile system, as circumstances bearing on whether good cause exists for a late filing or a late exemption request under Sec.  178.102(e)(2).
items.section: II. Public Comment Analysis – The Discretionary Exemption From Electronic Filing

items.headline: OPM declined tolling, fixed response deadlines, and dual-track filing
items.what_changes: OPM rejected codified tolling for system outages, a fixed response deadline for exemption requests, tolling on a timely exemption request, and deeming non-electronic submissions filed on their original date. It also rejected a permanent paper/email option for survivors, beneficiaries, retirees and pro se claimants, relying on the exemption process and agency-assisted filing option.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM has not adopted the requests to codify a fixed, non-discretionary tolling period for system outages (Comment 06) or a fixed response deadline for exemption requests (Comments 03 and 05).
items.section: II. Public Comment Analysis – The Discretionary Exemption From Electronic Filing

items.headline: Effective-date inconsistency in the DFR admitted as a drafting error
items.what_changes: The DFR preamble said the rule would take effect 45 days after the comment period expired, which conflicts with the September 29, 2026 date in the DATES caption. OPM calls the 45-day reference a drafting error and confirms September 29, 2026 as the effective date. Claims filed before that date are processed under the earlier requirements.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The reference to ``45 days'' was a drafting error.
items.section: II. Public Comment Analysis – Effective Date

items.headline: Rule treated as procedural, exempt from notice and comment
items.what_changes: OPM defends using the 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(A) procedural-rule exception, arguing the rule does not change who may file, the substantive standard, the evidence required, or any codified time limit. It treats the good-cause finding as an unnecessary alternative basis.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: That is the character of this rule: it prescribes the manner in which a claim is submitted without altering who may file a claim, the substantive standard OPM applies in deciding it, the evidence required to support it, or the duration of any codified time limit.
items.section: II. Public Comment Analysis – Use of the Direct Final Rule Procedure

items.headline: Claims not rejected solely for missing denying-official contact details
items.what_changes: Although 178.102(a)(2) asks for the name and contact details of the agency official who denied the claim, OPM says it will not reject or delay a claim solely because the claimant cannot supply details never given to them.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Consistent with OPM's existing practice under this part, a claim will not be rejected or delayed solely because a claimant cannot supply contact details for an individual agency official that were never provided to the claimant.
items.section: II. Public Comment Analysis – Contact Information for the Denying Agency Official

items.headline: eFile registration is consent to electronic service; technical failures weighed case by case
items.what_changes: OPM treats eFile registration as consent to electronic service and compares the duty to monitor case activity to reviewing paper mail. Where a technical failure of the system prevented receipt of a posting, OPM will weigh it case by case under good cause. Judicial review under 178.107(b) is said to remain available.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Registration as an eFiler constitutes consent to electronic service. The responsibility to monitor case activity under Sec.  178.102(e)(1)(v) is no different in kind from the obligation of a party who receives paper correspondence to review their mail.
items.section: II. Public Comment Analysis – Electronic Service and the Written Record

items.headline: PRA status of eFile information collection and revised burden estimate
items.what_changes: OMB approved the eFile collection under control number 3206-0282. The 30-day notice estimates 1,286 respondents and 13,039 annual burden hours, covering all appeal types in eFile. OPM says it never refused or delayed a claim or exemption request because of control-number status.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The 30-day notice (91 FR 46802 (July 24, 2026)) reflects a revised estimate of 1,286 respondents and 13,039 annual burden hours, which reflects the full scope of appeals available through the eFile system.
items.section: II. Public Comment Analysis – Paperwork Reduction Act Status of the eFile Information Collection

items.headline: Outdated office name left in 178.207(b) and (c) for later rulemaking
items.what_changes: The DFR removed the old 'Office of Merit Systems Oversight and Effectiveness' reference from 178.102(e) but left it in 178.207(b) and (c) for claims of money due deceased employees. OPM plans to update to Merit System Accountability and Compliance in a future rulemaking.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM intends to conform the cross-references in Sec.  178.207(b) and (c) to the office's current name, Merit System Accountability and Compliance, in a future rulemaking.
items.section: II. Public Comment Analysis – Cross-Reference to an Outdated Office Name

items.headline: Five comments, none significant adverse; no text change
items.what_changes: OPM received five timely comments, most opposing the rule, and found none significant adverse alone or together. It made no substantive change to the rule text and confirmed the effective date.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: None causes OPM to reevaluate the rule's underlying approach, none identifies a respect in which the rule as adopted would be ineffective or unacceptable absent a change to its text, and none has caused OPM to make a substantive change to the rule.
items.section: III. Determination Regarding Significant Adverse Comment

How long OPM will take to respond to exemption requests, since OPM declined to set a deadline.
What criteria OPM uses to decide whether a party 'cannot reasonably file electronically' beyond that phrase.
The date by which OPM will conform the outdated office-name cross-references in 178.207(b) and (c).
The identity or affiliation of the five commenters.
How many exemptions have been requested or granted since the effective date.

findings.plain_summary: OPM is issuing competency-based classification standards for eight administrative series (0301, 0306, 0308, 0340, 0341, 0343, 0346, 2291) covering about 220,000 positions, effective March 22, 2027. Agencies must inventory and review existing positions by November 29, 2027, may use human-validated SI tools to speed the review, and the matching qualification standards are not yet released.

items.headline: Standards take effect March 22, 2027; review of all existing positions due November 29, 2027
items.what_changes: The new standards supersede the prior classification standards for the eight series on March 22, 2027. New and reclassified positions must follow them by that date, and agencies must finish reviewing all existing positions in the covered series by November 29, 2027. Mission-critical prioritization may set the review order but does not extend the completion date.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Apply them to new and reclassified positions in the covered series no later than March 22, 2027, and complete the review of existing positions in the covered series no later than November 29, 2027.

items.headline: About 220,000 positions fall under the eight covered series
items.what_changes: OPM states the scale of positions governmentwide that the standards cover. The agency review obligation applies across this population.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: These series encompass approximately 220,000 positions governmentwide — currently classified across the Federal government.

items.headline: Matching Group Qualification Standards not yet issued; existing qualification requirements stay in effect until then
items.what_changes: The competency-based qualification standards are still in development, with release expected by November 30, 2026. Existing group qualification requirements remain in effect until then. The standards take effect March 22, 2027, so agencies will be applying new classification standards alongside qualification standards that are separate and not yet published.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM will issue the corresponding Competency Based Group Qualification Standards separately. They are still in development, and OPM expects to release them by November 30, 2026.
items.section: Memorandum body (effective date and qualification standards)

items.headline: FAQ deadline of '120 days after the date of this issuance' does not match the memo's dates
items.what_changes: The FAQ sets the new-and-reclassified-position deadline at 120 days after the November 16, 2026 issuance, which falls about March 16, 2027, not the March 22, 2027 date in the memo body. The memo also refers to a '365-day window' for existing-position review, but November 29, 2027 is not 365 days from either November 16, 2026 or March 22, 2027. The document does not reconcile these.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Agencies should apply the standards to new and reclassified positions no later than 120 days after the date of this issuance and complete the implementation tasks within the windows set out in the Implementation for the Covered Series section.

items.headline: Inventory must include positions in adjacent series, not just the eight covered series
items.what_changes: Agencies must inventory all encumbered and vacant positions in the covered series. They must also include positions in adjacent series whose duties may fall within the revised occupational definitions, which widens the review beyond the 220,000-position figure.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Inventory all encumbered and vacant positions currently classified in the covered series, along with positions in adjacent series whose duties may fall within the revised occupational definitions.
items.section: Implementation for the Covered Series, step 1

items.headline: Reclassification required only where review shows the current classification no longer fits
items.what_changes: The review is mandatory for existing positions, but a classification action is required only when the series, title, or grade no longer reflects the work. Many positions are expected to need only documented confirmation.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Reclassification is required only where the review shows that a position's current series, title, or grade no longer reflects the work performed under the revised standard.

items.headline: Employee notice, appeal, and pay-setting protections preserved; no retroactive application
items.what_changes: Any resulting series, title, or grade change is processed under existing procedures. OPM states the issuance does not alter employee entitlements and that the standards are not intended to apply retroactively to completed personnel actions.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Nothing in this issuance changes an employee's entitlement to those protections, and nothing in the revised standards is intended to be applied retroactively to completed personnel actions.

items.headline: SI-assisted review allowed but human approval required for every determination
items.what_changes: Agencies may use SI, text-analysis tools, or USA Class to speed the review, but the tools only triage and prioritize. No classification, titling, grading, or qualification decision may rest on an SI result a qualified human has not examined and approved. The governing toolkit is published separately and not attached.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: No classification, titling, grading, or qualification determination should rest on an SI-generated result that a qualified human reviewer has not examined and approved.
items.section: Implementation for the Covered Series, step 3

items.headline: Degree requirements not treated as automatic proxies for ability
items.what_changes: The qualification approach cites the Merit Hiring Plan and Executive Orders 13932 and 14170. Degrees are not automatic proxies for ability, though where a degree is required by law agencies will validate the education along with the skills.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Consistent with the Merit Hiring Plan and Executive Orders 13932 and 14170, degree requirements are not treated as automatic proxies for ability.

items.headline: Series 2291 Telecommunications replaces the former 0391 series
items.what_changes: The covered list includes a renumbered series, with 2291 identified as formerly 0391. The standards include crosswalks and descriptions of superseded series and titles, so some positions may change series, but the document gives no conversion details.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: 2291, Telecommunications (formerly the 0391 series)

items.headline: Comments must be consolidated by agency and reflect headquarters-level priorities
items.what_changes: Agencies must submit one consolidated comment set from all components through a survey link rather than component-level comments. The comments feed the next cycle, and OPM wants them to reflect headquarters-level priorities.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Consolidated comments should reflect headquarters-level priorities so that OPM can align the standards with your agency's mission-critical requirements.

could_not_determine: The text of the eight classification standards themselves, including the Factor Level Descriptions and crosswalks, which are listed as attachments but not included in this document.

Whether union notice or bargaining obligations apply beyond the general reference to existing agency procedures.

findings.plain_summary: OPM confirms that its direct final rule revising the early-commencement reduction factors for FERS survivor annuities of spouses of deceased separated employees took effect August 24, 2026, after it judged that none of the 7 comments were significant adverse comments. The notice acknowledges that the revised factors produce lower benefit amounts for survivors who elect earlier payment, a result of the Board of Actuaries' revised demographic assumptions.

items.headline: Revised factors lower annuity amounts for survivors who choose early commencement
items.what_changes: OPM concedes that, compared to the prior factors, the updated table yields lower monthly benefits for survivors electing an earlier survivor annuity. The summary describes only a 'revision' of the table and does not say that benefits go down.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Compared to the previous factors, OPM agrees that the updated factors result in lower benefit amounts for those who elect to receive an earlier survivor annuity.

items.headline: OPM says it has no discretion to keep prior factors; statute requires updating when actuarial assumptions change
items.what_changes: OPM rejected the argument that the rule is controversial, stating that 5 U.S.C. 8461(i) requires it to change factors when Board assumptions change, so it cannot retain factors that no longer give actuarial equivalence. Change is driven by the Board's 2025 revised demographic assumptions (including mortality improvement), while economic assumptions (4.00 percent interest) were unchanged.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Section 8461(i) requires OPM to make corresponding changes to factors used to produce actuarially equivalent benefits when the applicable actuarial assumptions change. Accordingly, OPM does not have discretion to retain factors that no longer produce the required actuarial equivalence.

items.headline: BEDB installment factors deliberately left unchanged
items.what_changes: OPM explained that Basic Employee Death Benefit factors were not revised because the relevant economic assumption did not change and the 36-month installment option is not life-contingent (remaining payments go to the spouse's estate), so mortality changes do not affect it.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM did not revise the BEDB factors because the economic assumption relevant to that benefit did not change.

items.headline: The '1950 through 1966' column was removed because it can no longer apply
items.what_changes: In response to a commenter, OPM explained that the column for the 30-years-of-service table applied only to employees dying before minimum retirement age; the youngest in that birth range reached MRA in 2023, so the column is obsolete. Prior table versions remain available (88 FR 66679) and OPM would apply the appropriate version to older claims.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Accordingly, after 2023 no employee within the 1950-1966 birth range could die before reaching their minimum retirement age (MRA), which is the circumstance in which this column would be used.

items.headline: 7 comments received; none deemed significant adverse; no changes made
items.what_changes: Of 7 timely comments, 2 supported, 2 were unrelated, and 3 raised concerns (actuarial transparency, BEDB, benefit reduction), plus others on the removed column and lack of examples. OPM concluded none required reconsideration, new analysis, or substantive change, so the rule took effect as published. No examples of the effect on annuities were added; OPM said survivors get individualized figures during claims processing.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM has determined that none of the comments caused OPM to reconsider the rule, conduct additional actuarial analysis, or make a substantive change.

items.headline: No worked examples; survivors get personalized figures in claims process
items.what_changes: OPM declined to add illustrative examples to the rule, stating the amount depends on the deceased employee's age, service, and base annuity, and that survivors receive individualized annuity option amounts during claims.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM nevertheless agrees that individualized information is important and notes that survivors receive personalized information detailing annuity options, including amounts, during the claims process.

could_not_determine: How many survivors or claims are affected by the revised factors.
The actual numerical factors in the revised table, or the size of the reduction in monthly annuity amounts (no examples given).
The cost or savings to the CSRDF from the revision.
The specific demographic assumption changes (e.g., the mortality improvement figures) adopted by the Board of Actuaries.
Whether any pending or already-decided claims will be recalculated with the new factors, beyond the statement that the appropriate table version would be applied to older claims if needed.

findings.plain_summary: OPM confirms that its August 14, 2026 direct final rule removing or updating obsolete Civil Service Rules provisions (5 CFR parts 2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 10) took effect October 13, 2026, after it received four comments and judged none to be significant adverse comments. In responding, OPM rejected two commenters' requests to withdraw the rule, adopted one suggestion to add a no-reliance confirmation for removed Rule II provisions, and clarified that the rule changes no substantive rights and removes no Federal Register publication requirement.

items.headline: OPM rejects calls to withdraw rule and reissue as proposed rule
items.what_changes: Two commenters (04 and 05) labeled their comments significant adverse and asked OPM to withdraw the direct final rule and reissue it for notice and comment, arguing the E.O. 14410 authority citations legitimize Schedule Policy/Career and diminish tenure and appeal rights. OPM determined neither was significant adverse, saying they misread the rule and target actions in other proceedings, so the rule stays in effect without a new comment round.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Having considered both comments in full, OPM has determined that neither is a significant adverse comment. Both rest on a misreading of what the rule does, and both direct their objections at Presidential and regulatory actions taken in other proceedings that this rule neither effects nor alters.

items.headline: OPM states the rule changes no substantive rights or protections
items.what_changes: In response to Comment 02, OPM confirms that no amendment, removal, redesignation, or terminology change alters competitive status, veterans' preference, appointment or reinstatement eligibility, or adverse action, grievance, or appeal rights.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: First, OPM confirms that the direct final rule makes no change to any substantive right, obligation, or protection.

items.headline: Authority citations now cite E.O. 14410; OPM says they have no operative effect
items.what_changes: The rule revised the authority citations for parts 2, 3, 5, 6, 9, and 10 to cite E.O. 14410. OPM says a citation confers no authority and imposes no obligation, and that the rule does not amend § 6.2 or part 213 (the Schedule Policy/Career regulations). Its only Rule VI changes are the § 6.1(a) report reference and removal of the three grandfathering provisions in § 6.8(a)-(c), plus redesignation of § 6.8(d)-(e).
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The authority citation identifies the source of authority for the regulatory text; it confers no authority, imposes no obligation, and has no operative effect of its own.

items.headline: OPM says no Federal Register publication requirement was removed; adds FR as authorized venue
items.what_changes: OPM says the old §§ 3.2, 5.1, and 6.1(a) required publication only in OPM annual reports or the Federal Personnel Manual, which no longer exist, not in the Federal Register. Revised §§ 5.1(c) and 6.1(a) now add the Federal Register as an authorized publication venue, and § 6.1(c) and 5 CFR 213.103 FR requirements are left intact.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The rule therefore removes no Federal Register publication requirement. To the contrary, revised Sec.  5.1(c) and revised Sec.  6.1(a) add the Federal Register as an authorized publication where the prior text did not mention it,

items.headline: OPM adopts commenter's suggestion: confirms nothing depends on removed Rule II provisions
items.what_changes: OPM adds a confirmation that no current positions, incumbents, appointments, or agency operations depend on the provisions removed at 5 CFR 2.1(c), 2.2(a)(4), and 2.3, citing the Postal Reorganization Act of 1970 and the 1978 repeal of the apportionment requirement formerly in 5 U.S.C. 3306.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM adopts the suggestion. For the reasons stated in the direct final rule with respect to Civil Service Rule II, 91 FR at 52475-76, OPM confirms that no current positions, incumbents, appointments, or agency operations depend on the provisions removed at 5 CFR 2.1(c), 2.2(a)(4), and 2.3.

items.headline: OPM declines to build public repository or posting timelines for 5 CFR 5.1 variations
items.what_changes: OPM declined the request for a centralized, permanent, searchable repository with defined posting periods for variations, calling website design, retention, and timelines outside the scope of the rule. It says the four elements the Director must note in the official record for each variation were retained without substantive change.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The commenter's further recommendations concerning the design, retention practices, and posting timelines of OPM's website concern the administration of the website rather than the text of Civil Service Rule V and are outside the scope of this rule.

items.headline: 3.1(b) disability-terminology revision confirmed as terminology-only
items.what_changes: OPM confirms the revised § 3.1(b) keeps the same three employee classes, the two-year satisfactory service in the excepted service requirement, and the agency-recommendation predicate, and does not narrow eligibility to acquire competitive status.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: It does not narrow eligibility, alter any substantive standard, or reduce any opportunity to acquire competitive status.

items.headline: Removal of 6.8(a)-(c) is prospective; prior actions remain governed by law then in effect
items.what_changes: OPM says the removal of the obsolete grandfathering paragraphs does not affect interpretation of personnel actions taken while they were in effect, and the rationale is in the direct final rule preamble.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Prospective removal of these paragraphs does not affect the interpretation of personnel actions taken while they were in effect; those actions remain governed by the law in effect when they were taken, and the text of prior editions of the Code of Federal Regulations remains publicly available.

items.headline: Effective date confirmed as October 13, 2026; four comments received
items.what_changes: The direct final rule took effect on schedule on October 13, 2026, because OPM received no significant adverse comment among four comments (two supportive, two opposed).
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM did not receive a significant adverse comment on the direct final rule. Accordingly, OPM confirms that the amendments published at 91 FR 52475 on August 14, 2026, became effective on October 13, 2026.

could_not_determine: How many positions, employees, or agencies, if any, are affected by the removed or updated provisions (OPM states none currently depend on them, but gives no counts).
The full list of specific regulatory text changes; this confirmation document contains no amendatory text and refers readers to 91 FR 52475.
Whether any of the four commenters will seek judicial review or otherwise challenge the rule or E.O. 14410.
What OPM will do about the commenter's request for a permanent, searchable website repository of 5 CFR 5.1 variations, beyond calling it outside the scope of the rule.

stories.headline: New skills-based classification standards for eight administrative series, about 220,000 positions
stories.takeaway: New competency-based classification standards supersede prior standards for eight administrative series covering about 220,000 positions on March 22, 2027, and agencies must review all existing positions by November 29, 2027. The FAQ's 120-day deadline (about March 16, 2027) and the memo's '365-day window' do not match the memo's stated dates.

stories.headline: Mandatory eFile now required for FLSA and other administrative claims
stories.takeaway: FLSA claims and certain administrative claims must be filed through eFile as of September 29, 2026, unless OPM grants a discretionary exemption. OPM will not find good cause for a late settlement-claim filing if no exemption was requested before the deadline, and it declined to toll deadlines while exemption requests are pending, though requests may be made by phone or email.

stories.headline: Revised FERS factors cut early survivor annuities for separated employees' spouses
stories.takeaway: The revised early-commencement factors, effective August 24, 2026, yield lower monthly benefits for spouses of deceased separated employees who elect an earlier survivor annuity. OPM says 5 U.S.C. 8461(i) requires the update after the Board of Actuaries' 2025 revised demographic assumptions.

stories.headline: Civil Service Rules cleanup takes effect despite withdrawal demands
stories.takeaway: The rule removing obsolete Civil Service Rules provisions took effect October 13, 2026; OPM rejected two commenters' demands to withdraw it over E.O. 14410 authority citations. OPM says the citations have no operative effect, the rule does not amend § 6.2 or part 213, and no substantive rights or protections change.
